purpose: The 50 curated realistic advocate research tasks behind the product North Star: LawMind Research Task Completion Rate - the advocate finds the authority, verifies the source, reads enough context to use it, saves it to the matter, and finishes without another legal database.

thresholdPolicy.why: A threshold set before any advocate has attempted the set is a number invented to be met. The 3-5 advocate shadow beta in Sprint 3 (12-18 September) establishes the baseline.
thresholdPolicy.neverMovedAfter: Moving a threshold once results arrive is self-deception, and an investor can tell.

scopeGuard: This task set is NOT permission to revive broad semantic search, build Gold V3, or turn NEW3 into a retrieval-evaluation lane. It measures whether an advocate finishes a task. It does not measure recall@k, and no task in it requires the semantic arm.

construction.legalContentRule: No task asserts a section number, a holding, or a court-hierarchy fact. Every task is a description of what an advocate is TRYING TO DO. Where a statute or section is needed, the advocate supplies it from their own brief - which is also how it happens in practice.
construction.expectedFailures: 4 tasks are included that are EXPECTED TO FAIL on current capability, and each says so and why. They are in the set deliberately: a task set containing only things that work measures nothing, and it would hide from the shadow beta exactly the gaps a beta exists to find.
construction.enabledIsNotTheSameAsCompletable: Worth reading carefully: 48 of the 50 tasks point at a capability the registry marks ENABLED_V1, yet FOUR are expected to fail. Only ONE of those four (RT-44, old/new code correspondence) points at a DISABLED row. The other three fail INSIDE an enabled capability - currentness coverage is five judgments, treatment provenance is not on the wire, statute freshness is UNMEASURED. A capability being ENABLED means the product does the thing; it does not mean an advocate can finish the task. That gap is exactly what a task-completion metric measures and a capability registry cannot.

progress.nextStep: Shadow beta, 12-18 September, 3-5 practising advocates, observed sessions. Score each task attempted / completed-without-leaving / completed-with-help / failed.

tasks.task: Open the judgment for a neutral citation written on a brief.
tasks.completeWhen: The judgment opens and its citation matches the one typed, character for character.

tasks.task: Open a judgment from a reporter citation an opponent cited in writing.
tasks.completeWhen: The judgment opens, or the product says plainly that it does not hold that reporter citation.

tasks.task: Find a case when only the CNR number is known, from a client file.
tasks.completeWhen: The judgment or its record opens from the CNR alone.

tasks.task: Find a case from a case number and year written in a cause list.
tasks.completeWhen: Every judgment matching that case number is shown, without one being guessed as the right one.

tasks.task: Find a case from its full cause title as printed on an order.
tasks.completeWhen: The judgment resolves at rank 1, or every candidate sharing that title is offered.

tasks.task: Find a case remembered only by the parties' names.
tasks.completeWhen: The authority is reachable from the party names alone, or the product says the name is too common and asks for one more detail.
tasks.note: Measured 30 Aug: works for a name with a distinguishing token; refuses at 1,239 ms for a name of only common tokens.

tasks.task: Distinguish two judgments that share a cause title.
tasks.completeWhen: Both are shown with enough on the row - court, date, case number - to tell them apart without opening either.

tasks.task: Confirm that a citation an opponent gave actually exists.
tasks.completeWhen: The product either produces the judgment or states that it cannot confirm it exists. It never implies the citation is fake, and never implies it is real.

tasks.task: Find the later order in a matter when only the earlier judgment is held.
tasks.completeWhen: Other records sharing the case number are reachable from the one in hand.

tasks.task: Check whether a judgment cited in a textbook is one we hold at all.
tasks.completeWhen: A clear held / not-held answer. "Not held" is a complete answer and is not a failure of the task.

tasks.task: Read what one High Court decided on a broad subject in the last month.
tasks.completeWhen: Results return for one named court and a short window.
tasks.note: Measured: one court + one month returns results in 418 ms; a court CATEGORY does not.

tasks.task: Restrict a search to a single named High Court.
tasks.completeWhen: Only that court appears in the results and the filter is visibly applied.

tasks.task: Restrict a search to a date range around a known hearing.
tasks.completeWhen: The range is honoured and an empty range says so rather than returning neighbours.

tasks.task: Search a term that turns out to be too common, and recover.
tasks.completeWhen: The refusal names a remedy that actually works - a single court, a shorter range - and following it returns results.
tasks.note: The refusal must NOT offer a court category as the remedy. Measured: categories are still refused.

tasks.task: Search only Supreme Court authority on a point.
tasks.completeWhen: The court filter is applied and the results are visibly Supreme Court only.

tasks.task: Find recent authority in a court where we hold little.
tasks.completeWhen: The product says the filter has no data behind it, rather than returning zero results as if none exist.

tasks.task: Combine a court filter and a case-type filter.
tasks.completeWhen: Both apply, and a combination with no data says so.

tasks.task: Search with a phrase from a judgment already in hand.
tasks.completeWhen: The source judgment is reachable from its own words.

tasks.task: Ask something the product cannot answer, and find out quickly.
tasks.completeWhen: A refusal arrives fast and states why. Never "no judgments matched" where nothing was searched.

tasks.task: Understand whether an empty result means nothing exists or nothing was searched.
tasks.completeWhen: The two are visibly different states. This is the single most important task in the set.

tasks.task: Read enough of a judgment to decide whether to cite it.
tasks.completeWhen: The operative reasoning is readable without leaving the product.

tasks.task: See where a judgment came from before relying on it.
tasks.completeWhen: The source is named and its currentness shown, on the same screen as the text.

tasks.task: Tell a document we hold from a link to a document we do not.
tasks.completeWhen: The two render differently and the difference is legible without explanation.

tasks.task: Notice that a judgment is image-only before quoting it.
tasks.completeWhen: The image-only state announces itself and is never presented as text evidence.

tasks.task: Find out how current the corpus is for the court being researched.
tasks.completeWhen: A per-court freshness answer, not a single corpus-wide date.

tasks.task: Copy a passage accurately for a written submission.
tasks.completeWhen: The passage copies as the court wrote it, with no silent normalisation.

tasks.task: Read a Hindi-script judgment without the script breaking.
tasks.completeWhen: Devanagari renders correctly. This is a rendering task, not a translation task.
tasks.note: Hindi SEMANTIC capability is POST_V1 and no task here tests it.

tasks.task: Decide not to rely on a judgment because the evidence is withheld.
tasks.completeWhen: The withheld state is explicit and the advocate stops, correctly, rather than quoting a truncated document.

tasks.task: Check whether an authority is still good law before filing.
tasks.completeWhen: The LAW MOVED state is shown where it applies, read live. Where nothing is recorded, the product does not imply the authority is safe.
tasks.expectedToFail: Canonical-safe currentness coverage is FIVE judgments. This task is expected to reveal how little we can say, and that is the finding.

tasks.task: See that an authority has been overruled before citing it.
tasks.completeWhen: The mark appears on every surface the authority appears on, including inside a matter.

tasks.task: Learn who recorded that an authority was overruled - a court or a law reporter.
tasks.completeWhen: The source of the treatment is visible.
tasks.expectedToFail: treatment_provenance is not on the wire. CCR-2026-08-30-05, DEFERRED to Gate C. This task is expected to FAIL in the shadow beta and is included so the failure is measured rather than assumed.

tasks.task: Notice a citation the product could not confirm.
tasks.completeWhen: The unverified mark is unmissable and offers the eCourts path. It is never silently dropped.

tasks.task: Understand that a verified citation carries no badge.
tasks.completeWhen: Silence reads as confidence, not as omission. If a beta advocate reads silence as "not checked", that is a P0 finding about the design.

tasks.task: See which cases cite an authority in hand.
tasks.completeWhen: Inbound citations are shown WITH their coverage block, so partial reads as partial.

tasks.task: Avoid treating a partial citation graph as a complete one.
tasks.completeWhen: No count is presented as a total.

tasks.task: Refrain from adding a set-aside authority to a matter.
tasks.completeWhen: add-to-matter is disabled for set_aside, and the reason is stated.

tasks.task: Find out that we hold no citation data for a judgment.
tasks.completeWhen: Absence reads as absence of data, never as an invalid judgment.

tasks.task: Decide whether a reported treatment is strong enough to act on.
tasks.completeWhen: The advocate can see the basis and reach their own view. The product does not conclude for them.

tasks.task: Open a section of an Act by name and number from a brief.
tasks.completeWhen: The section opens with its temporal state visible.

tasks.task: Find judgments that reference a specific section.
tasks.completeWhen: Linked judgments are listed, with the known precision defect stated rather than hidden.

tasks.task: Check whether a section was in force on the date of the offence.
tasks.completeWhen: Commencement and amendment state are readable.
tasks.note: ENGINEERING STORES TEMPORAL FACTS. A legal applicability conclusion requires legal sign-off and the product must not draw one.

tasks.task: Work out the new-code counterpart of an old-code section.
tasks.completeWhen: Either a correspondence is shown with its basis, or the product says it cannot answer.
tasks.expectedToFail: statute.old_new_correspondence is DISABLED_NOT_READY. Expected to fail. BNS/BNSS/BSA replaced IPC/CrPC/Evidence in July 2024 and no automatic applicability conclusion may be drawn without legal sign-off.

tasks.task: Find how current our statute data is.
tasks.completeWhen: A freshness answer, or an explicit UNMEASURED.
tasks.expectedToFail: Statute freshness is UNMEASURED. NEW2 Sprint-3 bounded measurement.

tasks.task: Create a matter for a live case.
tasks.completeWhen: The matter is created and reopens with its details intact.

tasks.task: Save an authority found in research into that matter.
tasks.completeWhen: The authority is saved and listed with its three citation fields read live.

tasks.task: Return the next day and find the saved authority still current.
tasks.completeWhen: overruled_status is read at render, so an authority that moved overnight shows it. It is never cached.

tasks.task: Keep authorities for two different clients from mixing.
tasks.completeWhen: Matters are isolated. A confidentiality failure here is the most serious defect in the set.

tasks.task: Record the next hearing date from the advocate's own file.
tasks.completeWhen: The manual path is first-class and does not read as a second-best substitute for a lookup we cannot do.

tasks.task: Complete a whole research task without leaving LawMind.
tasks.completeWhen: Search to reader to saved authority to matter, with no other legal database opened. THIS IS THE NORTH STAR TASK.

tasks.task: Find the authority saved last week without remembering its name.
tasks.completeWhen: Saved authorities are browsable inside the matter.
